audit.title: Payment Modes
audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured conceptual page that explains the three DTA settlement models with a strong up-front comparison table and consistent entity naming. Its biggest GEO strength is that table plus disciplined section boundaries; its biggest opportunity is discoverability — the page carries no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no dates, and no question/symptom-phrased headings, so a well-written explanation risks never being retrieved. The honest verdict: solid prose, under-instrumented for machines, and thin on the concrete specifics (supported chains, CCIP mechanics, atomicity guarantees) that generative engines preferentially cite.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema, canonical URL, and dateModified
recommendations.change: Emit a `TechArticle` block with `headline`, `about` (DTA, CCIP, fund settlement), canonical `https://docs.chain.link/dta-technical-standard/concepts/payment-modes`, and a visible `dateModified`.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals are direct E-E-A-T inputs that raise parse-ability and trust for retrieval.

recommendations.title: Add a decision-oriented, question-phrased heading and section
recommendations.issue: No heading matches "which DTA payment mode should I use?"
recommendations.change: Add an H2 "Which payment mode should I choose?" with a 3-bullet decision rule: offchain if payment settles via bank wire; local onchain if all contracts + tokens are on one chain; cross-chain onchain if Request Management and Settlement are on different chains.
recommendations.why: devs/agents query by decision and symptom, not concept title; question-phrased sections win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics to each model
recommendations.issue: No supported networks, CCIP mechanics, or atomicity guarantees quantified.
recommendations.change: State which chains DTA supports, whether local settlement is a single atomic transaction (name it explicitly), and for cross-chain name the CCIP message type (token-transfer + data), and any finality/confirmation dependency.
recommendations.why: quantitative, version/network-specific claims are among the highest-lift changes for citation rate.

recommendations.title: Add descriptive alt text / a text summary for each diagram
recommendations.change: Replace placeholder with alt text describing the flow (already partly present in captions); ensure the caption text is real page text, not baked into the image.
recommendations.why: engines cannot lift a flow from an untagged image; the numbered steps carry it but alt text reinforces retrieval.

recommendations.title: Lead each section with the discriminating condition
recommendations.issue: "This model is designed for funds that handle payments through traditional… channels."
recommendations.change: Open with the trigger fact, e.g. "Use offchain settlement when monetary settlement happens outside the chain; DTA escrows tokens until the Transfer Agent confirms payment." Do the same for local (same-chain) and cross-chain.
recommendations.why: the first liftable sentence should carry the canonical selection fact so skimmed/RAG chunks answer correctly.

recommendations.title: Add inline external citations
recommendations.issue: 0 external links; CCIP referenced only as `/ccip`.
recommendations.change: Link "Chainlink CCIP" to the CCIP architecture/concepts page, and link the token-compliance mention to the relevant token-standard doc (e.g. the DTA standard spec / ERC-3643).
recommendations.why: inline authoritative references raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Add a one-sentence canonical definition of DTA
recommendations.issue: DTA is named but not crisply defined.
recommendations.change: Add: "The Digital Transfer Agent (DTA) standard is a set of onchain contracts that coordinate fund subscription and redemption between Transfer Agents, Fund Administrators, and Distributors."
recommendations.why: a self-contained definition near first use is preferentially lifted verbatim.

antiPatterns: Placeholder image references ("(Image: Image)") with no machine-readable alt text.
One vague quantifier ("most") where a concrete claim would score better.
No dates on a technical-standard page — freshness cannot be assessed by an engine.
offPageNotes: The page correctly points to `/llms.txt`; confirm this page is listed there for agent discovery.
Canonical/JSON-LD emission is likely a site-template concern — fix at the docs framework level so all `dta-technical-standard` pages inherit it.
`<head>` was not captured by the CLI; pass raw `<head>` in future runs to verify og/twitter/canonical tags rather than infer absence.
